design_rationale: Participants with psychological distress were explicitly randomly allocated to E-EPA or matching placebo using computer-generated, MDE-history-stratified randomization lists ("Stratified randomization lists were computer-generated by a statistician and given to the hospital's pharmacy"), in a double-blind placebo-controlled trial registered as ISRCTN69617477.

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated stratified randomization lists held by the hospital pharmacy (allocation concealed from researchers, who assigned next available entry number), and baseline characteristics were balanced apart from one chance difference in marital status, which was shown not to affect results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Stratified randomization lists were computer-generated by a statistician and given to the hospital's pharmacy. The researchers were responsible for seeing participants allocated the next available entry number into the trial, and each woman received her capsules directly from the pharmacist."

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding was intended and guess rates did not differ, but 50% of E-EPA versus 6% of placebo participants reported a fishy taste and significantly more adverse events, so blinding was likely partially broken for subjective self-rated outcomes; analysis was intention-to-treat, mitigating concerns.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "However, 50.0% of women in the E-EPA group stated that the capsules had a fishy taste compared with 5.9% in the placebo group (P < 0.0001)."

domain_judgments.rationale: 11.7% dropout overall with differential loss (16.4% placebo vs 6.8% E-EPA) and dropouts differed in baseline HAM-D-21; sensitivity analysis (last observation carried forward) was only applied to 2 women, so some risk of bias from missingness remains, particularly in the small stratified subgroups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Although not significant, a higher proportion of women in the placebo group than in the E-EPA group did not complete the 4-wk (14.8% compared with 5.1%; P = 0.0775) and 8-wk (16.4% compared with 6.8%; P = 0.1010) follow-up."

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated scales were applied identically in both arms and clinician assessors were trained and blinded, but the primary outcomes are self-reported and participants in the active arm could infer allocation from fishy taste/eructation, which could influence subjective ratings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Subjects, investigators, and staff were blinded to treatment assignment until the last participants completed the study."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and the pre-specified primary analysis (PGWB in all women) was null; the headline positive findings come from post hoc stratification by baseline MDE status across multiple scales and adjusted models (covariates such as fish aftertaste eructation), i.e., a subgroup analysis that appears not to have been pre-specified in the protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Assuming that the treatment effect might be different depending on the severity of the mood disorder at entry, we first tested the interaction between group and diagnosis of MDE at baseline... Therefore, the analyses were stratified by MDE diagnosis at baseline."

overall_summary: Randomization and allocation concealment were well executed and analyses were intention-to-treat, but the primary pre-specified comparison was null and the reported benefit derives from an apparently post hoc subgroup stratification by baseline MDE status across several scales (D5 high). Partial unblinding due to fishy taste/eructation and modest differential attrition add further concerns, yielding an overall high risk of bias.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly reports a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in which patients, stratified by antidepressant use, were "randomly allocated in two subgroups that had received either 4 capsules of omega-3 ... or mineral oil (placebo)", with randomization and capsule coding performed in a separate laboratory.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization with stratification by antidepressant use and off-site capsule coding suggests concealment, but the actual sequence-generation method is not described and baseline comparability is reported only for age, sex and depression scores in a very small sample (n=29).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The groups were then randomly allocated in two subgroups ... the randomization, identification of the groups and separation of the respective capsules were carried through in the neurophysiology laboratory of Universidade Federal do Paraná."

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding with identical capsules was maintained, but fish oil can cause recognizable taste/eructation effects, blinding success was not tested, adherence was only monitored by monthly capsule delivery, and the analysis excluded the 2 withdrawals rather than following intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The capsules containing fish oil or placebo were identical ... The study was double-blind, so that neither the researcher nor the patients knew which substance would be used as supplementation."

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 2/31 (7%) participants were lost with reasons given, but they were excluded from analysis without imputation, and in such small groups even two exclusions (plus the protocol rule excluding patients whose Hoehn & Yahr worsened) could influence effect estimates; lipid-profile data were also missing for most patients.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "two protocol breaks had occurred, followed by discontinuity in the research: one due to intestinal indisposition and another one due to an orthopedic column surgery ... These patients were excluded from the efficacy analysis."

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated depression scales were applied identically to all groups by the same trained assessor who was blinded to allocation under the double-blind design, making outcome ascertainment bias unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "the patients were evaluated by a trained psychologist (TMS) through Montgomery–Asberg Depression Scale (MADRS) ... The MADRS was considered the primary outcome variable"

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or pre-specified analysis plan is mentioned, and after the primary between-group BDI analysis was null the authors switched to alternative operationalizations (percentage change, within-group t-tests, one-tailed p-values), indicating selective reporting of favourable analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "(Fisher test= 3.39, P=0.075, two-tailed; P=0.04; one-tailed)" ... "when the percentage change in scores from baseline to endpoint was carried out, the groups (W3 and W3+AD) showed greater percentage reduction"

overall_summary: Although this small double-blind pilot trial used identical placebo capsules, blinded assessment with validated scales, and had minimal attrition, the absence of any pre-registration/analysis plan combined with post hoc switching to percentage-change outcomes, within-group tests and one-tailed p-values after null primary between-group results indicates a high risk of selective reporting. Unclear sequence generation and non-intention-to-treat analysis in a very small sample add further concerns, yielding an overall high risk of bias.

design_rationale: Explicit parallel-group RCT: "An independent, study-blinded statistician prepared a computer-generated randomization scheme allowing for randomization in blocks," with 35 patients randomized to n-3 PUFA (n=18) or placebo (n=17).

domain_judgments.rationale: About one third of randomized participants did not complete the trial (and only 25 of 35 contributed any post-baseline data to the "ITT-LOCF" primary analysis), with LOCF imputation and no sensitivity analyses demonstrating robustness to missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "only 24 patients (12 in each group; 66.7 vs. 70.6%, p = 0.083) completed this trial per protocol" ... "The sample size was small, and a large proportion of participants failed to complete the trial, which resulted in limited power"

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding and matched placebo were in place and an intention-to-treat (LOCF) analysis was the stated primary analysis, but the significantly higher rate of fishy eructation suggests possible functional unblinding, and co-intervention with heterogeneous antidepressants/usual care was not standardized.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Fishy burp was reported by three patients (30%) in the n-3 PUFA group and one patient (8%) in the placebo group, which was significant (p = 0.03)." ... "All study personnel and patients remained blinded to the identity codes throughout the course of the study."

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated depression scales applied identically in both groups by a blinded psychiatrist, but subjective clinician/self-report outcomes combined with possible unblinding via fishy burp, and internal inconsistency in reporting which CGI measure improved, leave some concern.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "CES-D-K... HAM-D-17... CGI-S... and CGI-I scores were measured by a psychiatrist who was blinded to treatment groups."

domain_judgments.rationale: Sequence generation and allocation concealment were adequately described, but there were notable baseline imbalances (fish intake p=0.025 and significantly different baseline depression severity in the analyzed ITT-LOCF population), which in a 35-patient trial raises some concern even if attributable to chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "An independent, study-blinded statistician prepared a computer-generated randomization scheme allowing for randomization in blocks... Identity codes were concealed in sequentially numbered opaque envelopes" ... "fish intake was greater in the placebo group than in the n-3 PUFA group at baseline" ... "CES-D-K (28.17 ± 2.46 vs. 35.69 ± 3.28)... scores were significantly (p < 0.001) different between the n-3 PUFA and placebo groups based on ITT analysis with LOCF"

domain_judgments.rationale: The pre-specified primary outcome (CES-D-K) was null and the conclusion rests on a covariate-adjusted secondary CGI result, with contradictory reporting of CGI-I versus CGI-S, apparently retrospective registration (trial ran 2010–2013; registered post hoc), and multiple outcome/analysis options, indicating selective reporting of a favourable result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Supplementation with n-3 PUFAs significantly (p = 0.041) reduced CGI-S score after adjustment for energy, fat, and fish intake as compared with the placebo group over the intervention period, but did not improve CES-D-K, HAM-D-17, or CGI-S scores" ... "This study was registered with the Clinical Research Information Service (KCT0001206)."

overall_summary: Although randomization and allocation concealment were well described and outcomes were rated by a blinded psychiatrist, the trial is at high risk of bias due to substantial attrition (~33% non-completion, LOCF imputation without sensitivity analyses) and selective reporting, with the null pre-specified primary outcome (CES-D-K) de-emphasized in favour of a covariate-adjusted secondary CGI result that is inconsistently labelled across the paper. Baseline imbalance in depression severity and fish intake plus possible unblinding from fishy eructation further compound concerns.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial with a coded (AB) block randomization table prepared by an independent statistician: "Bottles of identical oily preparation for each treatment group were assigned a participant number according to a coded (AB) block randomization table, prepared by an independent statistician."

domain_judgments.rationale: An independently prepared block randomization table with investigators blinded to codes supports adequate generation and concealment, but the method of generating the sequence is not described and some baseline imbalances are apparent (SF-36 mental function 61.2 vs 50.4, physical 45.0 vs 37.9; totally self-sufficient 11/22 vs 5/24), which are larger than one would comfortably attribute to chance and which directly bear on the outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Bottles of identical oily preparation for each treatment group were assigned a participant number according to a coded (AB) block randomization table, prepared by an independent statistician. Investigators were blinded to the randomization table, the code assignments, and the procedure."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, caregivers administering the supplement, and investigators were blinded by an identical lemon-flavored oily placebo, co-medication was held constant, no other depression treatment was given, and all 46 randomized participants appear analysed as allocated (22 vs 24).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "None of the studied patients complained of fish smell or fish eructation or made any comment about the content of the supplement she was taking or about the perception of having been included in 1 of the 2 groups, thus indicating the concealment of treatment allocation."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data appear available for all 46 randomized participants (22 and 24 at post-treatment, matching the numbers randomized), with no reported dropouts over the 8-week institutional trial, though only one baseline self-sufficiency value was missing.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Posttreatment Mean ± SD, n-3 Group (n = 22) ... Posttreatment Mean ± SD, Placebo Group (n = 24)"

domain_judgments.rationale: The GDS and SF-36 are validated instruments applied identically in both arms at weeks 0 and 8, outcome assessors/participants were blinded to allocation, and biochemical compliance analyses were explicitly "carried out blind to the participant status"; the self-report nature is mitigated by effective blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Depressive symptoms were assessed through the use of the GDS [33] before and after the treatment period (weeks 0 and 8). ... The validity and reliability of the test have been supported through both clinical practice and research evidence"

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or pre-specified analysis plan is cited, the responder threshold appears to have been defined post hoc ("we assumed"), both adjusted and unadjusted analyses are presented with the adjusted covariate set chosen by the authors, and some secondary results are reported only as "data not shown".
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Since n-3 LCPUFA supplementation could not be considered as an antidepressive therapy, we assumed that a 33% reduction in GDS score from baseline could be acceptable in evaluating response to supplementation."

overall_summary: The trial was well conducted in terms of blinding (identical lemon-flavoured placebo, blinded caregivers/investigators/lab), complete outcome data, and validated outcome measures, but concerns remain in two domains: incompletely described sequence generation with notable baseline imbalances in SF-36 scores and self-sufficiency, and the absence of pre-registration/pre-specified analysis plan with an apparently post hoc responder definition and author-selected covariate adjustment. Overall risk is therefore "some concerns", driven by Domains 1 and 5.

design_rationale: Explicit parallel-arm RCT with 1:1 allocation and a computer-generated block randomization code produced independently by the hospital pharmacy: "patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio" and "A block randomization code was independently computer generated at Sunnybrook Health Science Centre pharmacy." Registered as NCT00981383.

domain_judgments.rationale: Sequence generation (computer-generated block code) and concealment (pharmacy-prepared, consecutively prepackaged kits) were adequate, but several prognostically relevant baseline imbalances (age P=0.02, ASA P=0.03, baseline plasma EPA+DHA P=0.03, sMMSE P=0.06, diabetes) occurred, and block size/stratification were not reported, raising modest concern.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A block randomization code was independently computer generated at Sunnybrook Health Science Centre pharmacy. Kits with study medication were consecutively prepackaged as per the randomization sequence before commencement of the trial" ... "patients randomized to n-3 PUFA treatment were older, less likely to use acetylsalicylic acid, and more likely to be diabetic compared with those randomized to placebo. Omega-3 PUFA–treated patients also had lower mean sMMSE scores and lower plasma EPA + DHA concentrations at baseline"

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind design with a taste- and appearance-matched placebo, comparable adherence (median 92%, not different between arms) and adverse events across groups, and an ITT analysis with imputation; only one placebo patient withdrew for eructation, so deviations were minimal and balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All study personnel remained blind to treatment allocation until the database was 'locked.' ... The n-3 PUFA and placebo capsules were similar in appearance (dark brown) and taste (lemon-lime flavoring)." ... "An intention to treat (ITT) analysis of treatment efficacy was conducted"

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was low (11%) and balanced across arms with reasons documented and unrelated to the intervention, and missing data were handled by multiple imputation within an ITT framework.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Eighty-two (89%) of the randomized patients completed the trial. The dropout rate in the n-3 PUFA arm (n = 5) did not differ from that in the placebo arm (n = 5) (χ2 = 0.01, P = 0.94)." ... "Missing data from week 4, 8, and/or 12 assessments were imputed using a multiple imputation procedure (5 imputed data sets, as per Rubin)"

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated, appropriate outcome instruments were applied identically to both arms with blinded raters and analysts; self-reported BDI-II is blinded by the matched placebo, and practice effects were mitigated with alternate test forms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Depressive symptoms were measured using the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D). As recommended by expert consensus, the HAM-D is the gold standard for assessing antidepressant efficacy in trials with patients with CAD." ... "All analyses were performed blinded to treatment allocation and patient characteristics." ... "All cognitive testing was performed at a standardized time (900 hours ± 30 minutes)." ... "Alternate versions of each cognitive test were used at week 12 to minimize potential practice effects."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT00981383) with a clearly pre-specified primary outcome (HAM-D), and the null primary/secondary results are reported transparently; however, covariates were chosen post hoc from observed baseline imbalances, multiple cognitive domains and several unadjusted subgroup analyses were run, and the highlighted positive verbal-memory finding comes from an exploratory subgroup, so selective emphasis cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "For all analyses, covariates were selected based on significant and/or potentially clinically meaningful differenences in patient characteristics between the treatment groups at baseline." ... "In the subgroup of patients for whom baseline plasma EPA + DHA concentrations were available (post hoc analysis, n = 86)" ... "n-3 PUFAs significantly increased verbal memory compared with placebo in a subgroup of nondepressed patients"

overall_summary: This well-conducted, registered, double-blind placebo-controlled RCT had adequate allocation concealment, matched placebo, biochemically verified adherence, low and balanced attrition, ITT analysis with multiple imputation, and blinded validated outcome assessment. Overall risk is "some concerns" because of several prognostically relevant baseline imbalances (age, ASA use, diabetes, baseline sMMSE and plasma EPA+DHA) handled by post hoc covariate selection, and because the one positive result (verbal memory) arises from multiple exploratory cognitive outcomes and unregistered subgroup analyses in an underpowered sample.

design_rationale: Explicit 1:1:1 random allocation of 108 patients to two omega-3 formulations or matched placebo, with a computer-generated randomization schedule ("The randomization schedule was generated separately for each site in blocks of 12 using 'proc plan' in SAS"), double-blind and placebo-controlled.

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated, site-stratified block randomization produced by an external statistician and sent directly to the study pharmacist, ensuring allocation concealment; baseline characteristics were broadly similar (minor imbalances in LVEF, sex, NYHA class consistent with chance in a pilot sample).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The randomization schedule was generated separately for each site in blocks of 12 using 'proc plan' in SAS. This schedule was generated by an external statistician who was not involved with the OCEAN study and sent directly to the study pharmacist without involvement of the OCEAN study statistician."

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind with identical-appearing capsules and an appropriate intention-to-treat analysis for primary outcomes, but the authors acknowledge possible unblinding via fishy odor/GI side effects, and dose reductions (1–2 capsules in 19 patients) represent deviations; the emphasized per-protocol "completers" analyses are not ITT.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "the more prominent group disparity in the 'other' category (characterized by diarrhea/loose stools, itching/rash, and burping) suggests that some participants in the active treatment group may have guessed that they were receiving the active treatment."

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 8 participants withdrew early and primary endpoints were multiply imputed under ITT, but 25.9% failed to qualify as "completers" and the per-protocol/secondary analyses (including the highlighted SF-36 social functioning and correlation findings) were restricted to this unbalanced subset (26/22/26 of 36 per arm), with additional missing baseline outcome values.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "80 (74.1%) qualified as completers"; "N values ranged from 30 to 36 for baseline outcome measures by treatment arm due to missing data."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes used validated instruments (HAM-D, BDI-II, SF-36) and objective blinded laboratory RBC fatty acid assays applied identically across arms, but HAM-D is interviewer-administered and the self-report psychosocial measures are susceptible to the possible unblinding noted by the authors (who themselves cannot exclude a placebo effect).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "We also cannot rule out that the possible enhancement of social functioning may have arisen as a function of a placebo effect."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered (NCT02057406) with pre-specified primary endpoints and pre-specified per-protocol analyses, but a very large number of secondary/exploratory outcomes and subscale correlations were tested with no correction for multiple testing, and the null primary results are framed around selectively highlighted exploratory per-protocol findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "given the pilot nature of the study and this relatively low power to detect group differences, we elected to make no correction for multiple testing."

overall_summary: Randomization and allocation concealment were well executed and the primary ITT analysis of objective RBC omega-3 levels is robust, but some concerns arise for the psychosocial outcomes from possible unblinding via side effects, reliance on an incomplete "completers" subset for the positive findings, and extensive uncorrected multiple testing of exploratory outcomes. Overall risk is therefore judged "some concerns," driven by domains 2–5.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a "randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial" in which "Thirty-six depressed patients were randomly assigned to receive DHA, 2 g/day, or placebo for 6 weeks."

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment is stated but the sequence generation method and allocation concealment are not described, and there were statistically significant baseline imbalances (Hamilton score, smoking, weight) that the authors themselves flag as potentially influential.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The randomization produced some baseline differences between the two groups. It is conceivable that these differences contributed to the results of the study in an as yet not understood manner." ... "Baseline | 23.5 | 3.1 | 28.5 | 4.5 | 3.86 | 0.001"

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind and analyzed on an intent-to-treat basis with biochemically verified adherence, but the markedly different adverse-event profile (fish aftertaste in 14/18 DHA patients) could have unblinded participants and raters, and no formal blinding-integrity check is reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The reported adverse events in the DHA group included a 'fish' aftertaste (N=14), belching (N=3)... Compliance was confirmed by a twofold increase (t=8.40, df=19, p<0.0001) in red blood cell DHA levels"

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 35 of 36 randomized participants (97%), a single exclusion unlikely to bias results, and no participants withdrew due to adverse events.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Of the 36 participants who enrolled, 35 had at least one follow-up assessment and were included in this intent-to-treat analysis."

domain_judgments.rationale: The MADRS is an appropriate, validated clinician-rated measure applied identically to both arms, but it is assessor-dependent and the paper does not state that raters were independent/blinded beyond the general "double-blind" label, while the distinctive fishy aftertaste creates plausible unblinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale was the a priori primary outcome measure, and response was defined as a 50% or greater reduction in score from baseline to study endpoint."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome, response definition, and power calculation were specified a priori and reported, with secondary measures and a post hoc ANCOVA transparently presented alongside the null primary result, so selective reporting is unlikely despite the absence of a public pre-registration.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Response was defined a priori as a ≥50% reduction in the score on the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale." ... "This study was originally designed to detect a difference between groups in the change in Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale score from baseline to endpoint."

overall_summary: Overall risk is "some concerns," driven by unreported allocation sequence generation/concealment together with significant baseline imbalances (higher baseline Hamilton scores, smoking, and weight in the placebo arm) that the authors acknowledge may have affected results, and by potential unblinding from the distinctive fishy aftertaste affecting the clinician-rated outcome. Missing data were minimal and the a priori primary outcome was reported as planned, so no domain reaches high risk; however, the trial was also substantially underpowered (observed power 0.22), limiting confidence in the null finding.

design_rationale: Explicit parallel-group randomized allocation: "196 adults ... were randomized equally ... to 8 weeks of double-blind treatment with oral EPA-enriched n-3 1000 mg/d, DHA-enriched n-3 1,000 mg/d, or placebo," with allocation performed by institutional research pharmacies using permuted/fixed blocks.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was generated and held by independent research pharmacies with blocked randomization, concealed from staff via blind treatment codes, and baseline characteristics were balanced across the three arms except for a single chance-level difference in employment status (P = .041 among many comparisons).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Randomization and treatment assignment were carried out by the research pharmacies of both institutions by standard allocation procedures and a fixed block size of 30 subjects (MGH) or a randomly permuted block size between 6 and 15 subjects (CSMC). Only blind treatment codes, coordinated between both site pharmacies, were noted on randomization lists provided to study staff."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and all study staff were blinded, a double-dummy design preserved masking despite differing capsule appearance, adherence was monitored by pill count, and a modified intention-to-treat analysis with MMRM was used; only two discontinuations were attributable to the intervention experience.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A double-dummy placebo design was used to maintain the blind, since DHA-enriched capsules differed in appearance from EPA-enriched capsules... All study staff and participants remained blind to treatment assignment."

domain_judgments.rationale: 19 of 196 randomized subjects were excluded from the mITT sample for having no post-baseline visit and a further 13% of evaluable subjects did not complete; completion differed significantly by site and employment status, and MMRM assumes missingness at random without sensitivity analyses being reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Nineteen subjects dropped out before completing at least 1 postbaseline visit, leaving 177 evaluable subjects... Completers were more likely to be employed and to be from the CSMC site... the completion rate at CSMC was significantly higher than at MGH (93.5% vs 76.8%; χ2 1 = 10.39, P = .001)"

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (HDRS-17) is a standard validated clinician-rated depression measure applied identically at biweekly visits in all arms, with raters blinded to assignment and analyses conducted under blind treatment codes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Analyses of primary and secondary measures of depression severity were carried out based on blind treatment codes."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT00517036) with a clearly designated primary outcome and the null primary result is fully reported, but numerous unplanned subgroup analyses (baseline severity strata, comorbid anxiety, site) are emphasized without stated pre-specification or multiplicity correction, and recruitment was stopped early after a masked interim analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Other potential moderators of response (gender and presence/absence of comorbid anxiety disorder) were examined in relation to the primary outcome... However, a masked interim analysis indicated no treatment group difference, and continuing recruitment would unnecessarily expose subjects to unproven interventions."

overall_summary: This well-conducted, registered, double-blind, pharmacy-randomized placebo-controlled trial had strong allocation concealment, effective double-dummy blinding, and blinded standardized outcome assessment, but attrition before and during treatment (19 unevaluable plus 13% non-completion, with completion differing by site and employment) handled solely by MMRM, and post hoc subgroup/moderator analyses after early termination on an interim look, raise some concerns. No domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is "some concerns," driven by missing outcome data and potential selective reporting of secondary/subgroup results.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly reports a "randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial" in which "Randomization was carried out using the permuted block randomization procedure" with patients "randomly assigned into omega-3 or placebo groups."

domain_judgments.rationale: A permuted-block randomization procedure is stated and baseline demographic/clinical variables were similar between groups, but there is no description of sequence generation detail or of allocation concealment, and permuted blocks in an unblinded-staff, single-blind setting are potentially predictable.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Randomization was carried out using the permuted block randomization procedure. Patients were randomly assigned into omega-3 or placebo groups."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was only single-blind (care providers/investigators aware), the placebo lacked the fish-oil odour so participants may have guessed allocation, some omega-3 patients had dose reductions for GI effects, and the analysis was restricted to the 45 completers rather than intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Fifth, placebo capsules lacked omega-3 capsule odor that may affect the blindness of patients in the placebo arm of the study."

domain_judgments.rationale: Nine of 54 randomized patients (~17%) did not complete and were excluded from analysis; although reasons are shown in a flowchart, the per-arm attrition, reasons, and any sensitivity analysis for missingness are not described in the available text.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A total of nine patients failed to complete the study period... Thus, 45 patients (25 in the omega-3 group and 20 in the placebo group) completed the study and were included in final analysis."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome is a self-reported BDI score in a single-blind trial where blinding of participants may have been compromised by the absent fish-oil odour, so outcome reporting could be influenced by knowledge of allocation; laboratory markers were measured identically and objectively.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "our study used the self-reported BDI scale as a commonly validated and frequently used screening tool to rate depressive symptoms in HD patients"

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (IRCT201202203043N5), which is reassuring, but the pre-specified primary outcome and analysis plan are not stated, many outcomes/ratios and multiple regression models were analysed and reported (including post-hoc adjusted models emphasised when unadjusted comparisons were null), without correction for multiplicity.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "registered in Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (registry number: IRCT201202203043N5)"

overall_summary: All five RoB 2 domains raise some concerns: incompletely described allocation concealment, only single blinding with a placebo distinguishable by odour affecting a self-reported primary outcome, ~17% attrition analysed as completers only, and multiple outcomes/analyses without a stated pre-specified primary analysis. No single domain reaches high risk, so the overall judgment is some concerns.
